page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.8 is an x86_64 compute instance designed for enterprise applications requiring substantial memory allocation per compute unit. Powered by Intel Xeon 8167M processors operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, this configuration provides 8 physical cores mapped to 16 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 120.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.5 GB per vCPU, which positions it well above traditional general-purpose memory densities.

The instance does not bundle local NVMe or ephemeral storage disks, meaning all persistent data storage relies on external network-attached block volumes. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included. Networking features include one complimentary public IPv4 address alongside standard virtual cloud network integration.

Cost efficiency for VM.Standard2.8 is driven by its dense memory capacity relative to compute allocations. For environments where memory capacity is the primary constraint, this shape avoids the need to purchase larger core allocations simply to acquire necessary RAM. The tradeoff lies in the conservative 2.0 GHz clock speed of the older Intel Skylake architecture, making it less suited for single-thread CPU-bound tasks.

VM.Standard2.8 is suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including mid-tier in-memory caching layers, relational databases, enterprise resource planning backends, Java application runtimes, and distributed data processing nodes.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.8 is an x86_64 instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8167M processor running at 2.0 GHz. It provides 8 physical cores presenting 16 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core, coupled with 120.0 GB of system memory. This yields a high memory ratio of 7.5 GB per vCPU, well suited for workloads requiring substantial RAM footprint without necessitating higher core counts. The instance includes no onboard local storage, depending entirely on networked block storage for operating system and data requirements. There are no GPUs present. VM.Standard2.8 includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Its resource balance makes it an appropriate choice for mid-sized relational database servers, enterprise application runtimes, in-memory caches, and batch data processing where memory capacity requirements outweigh raw per-core CPU frequency demands.
